Is sports betting legal in North Carolina? The state law explained
Yes — regulated online sports wagering is legal here for adults aged 21 and over, under a specific statutory framework. Understanding that framework is what lets you tell a state-licensed app from an internationally licensed one.
The North Carolina Sports Wagering Act and its legislative framework
Session Law 2023-42, passed as House Bill 347, amended Chapter 18C of the General Statutes to authorize commercial mobile sports wagering statewide. The law sets out who may apply for a license, what they must pay, which wagers are permitted, and what consumer safeguards operators owe their customers. It also establishes a 23% tax on operators' gross wagering revenue — a levy on the licensed operator, not on your individual winning bets.
Before that law, sports wagering here existed only in limited retail form on tribal land. HB 347 created the commercial mobile market and put it under state supervision.
Operator obligations versus bettor position
This is the distinction that most confuses readers, so it is worth stating plainly. The statutory licensing obligations in Chapter 18C apply to operators. An unlicensed operator taking wagers from residents here is the party acting outside the state framework.
That does not mean an offshore account is equivalent to a licensed one from your side of the transaction. When you bet with an NCSLC-licensed operator, you have a regulator with jurisdiction over that operator, a defined complaints process, and state-mandated protections. When you bet with an internationally licensed book — every operator ranked on this page — you have whatever protections that book's own licensing jurisdiction provides, and no recourse through the NCSLC. Language on a site, dollar-denominated accounts, US payment options and an accessible website establish none of this either way. If a book is not on the Commission's licensee list, it is not state-licensed, full stop. Legal questions about your own position are for a qualified attorney, not a comparison site.
NCSLC licensing and the commercial partnership requirement
The Commission does not hand out mobile licenses on application alone. Under the Act, a prospective mobile operator must tie its license to a qualifying land-based partner — a professional sports team, a major sporting venue, or a motorsports facility within the state, or a tribal gaming operation. That structural requirement is why the licensed market here is a limited set of national brands attached to identifiable local partners rather than an open field.
Licensees also submit to background and financial suitability review, pay substantial application and renewal fees, and must implement approved geolocation technology that confirms a bettor is physically inside state lines at the moment a wager is placed.
Consumer protections written into the framework
Licensed operators must verify age and identity, enforce the 21-and-over threshold, segregate player funds from operating funds, offer responsible gambling controls, honor the statewide voluntary exclusion program, and follow advertising restrictions — including prohibitions on marketing aimed at minors and on describing wagers as risk-free when the customer's own money is at stake. A portion of state revenue from the framework is directed toward problem gambling treatment and education.
None of these obligations attach to an offshore operator. That is not a technicality; it is the single most important practical difference between the two categories.
How we reviewed the best NC sportsbooks on this page
Our assessment is a structured review of published information: operator terms and conditions, cashier documentation, licensing disclosures, promotional rules and publicly available corporate information. We did not conduct undercover deposits, timed withdrawal trials or support-response testing, and nothing on this page should be read as first-hand performance measurement. Where published evidence was insufficient, we said so in the relevant review instead of filling the gap with assumption.
The criteria we weighted, in rough order of importance for this comparison:
- Ownership and operating company. Who runs the book, under what corporate name, and whether that information is disclosed at all. Opaque ownership is a negative signal.
- Licensing credentials. Which authority licenses the operator and whether the license number is published and checkable. We treat international licensing as distinct from NCSLC authorization throughout.
- Terms and conditions quality. Whether bonus rules, void-bet policies, limit provisions and account-closure terms are specific and locatable, or vague and subject to unlimited discretion.
- Bonus fairness. Rollover multiple, whether it applies to bonus alone or deposit plus bonus, minimum-odds rules, market exclusions, expiry windows and maximum conversion caps.
- Payment flexibility. USD support, which card networks are accepted, which cryptocurrencies are supported, and whether withdrawal channels mirror deposit channels.
- Withdrawal caps and fees. Per-transaction and per-period payout limits, free withdrawal allowances, and charges beyond them.
- KYC requirements. What documentation is required, at what stage it is requested, and whether the policy is stated up front or sprung at first withdrawal.
- Customer support. Contact channels offered and stated hours. We report what is published; we did not time live-chat responses.
- Responsible gambling tools. Deposit and loss limits, session controls, cool-off options and self-exclusion, and how easy they are to find.
How we assess new NC betting sites and spot the warning signs
A genuinely new sportsbook is a new operating entity with no prior trading history. It is not the same thing as an established book that has changed domain, rebranded or shipped a redesigned interface — that happens routinely for reasons ranging from payment processing to marketing. Before treating a site as new, we look for the operating company behind it and its licensing record. Frequently, a "new" book turns out to be a long-running operator wearing a fresh skin, which is a materially different risk profile.
Where a book really is new, we say directly that limited history constrains what can be assessed. Nobody can evaluate payout reliability across a market cycle for a site that has not lived through one. Promising terms are not the same as a demonstrated record.
The specific red flags we weigh against a site:
- Hidden ownership. No named operating company, no registered address, no corporate detail anywhere in the terms or footer.
- Missing or unverifiable licensing. A regulator's logo with no license number, or a number that leads nowhere.
- Predatory withdrawal caps. Low weekly or monthly payout ceilings that would take months to release a mid-sized win, or caps disclosed only after registration.
- Inconsistent promotional rules. Landing-page terms that conflict with the full T&Cs, or bonus conditions that change without a version date.
- Unlimited discretionary clauses. Terms permitting the operator to void wagers or confiscate balances at sole discretion without defined grounds.
- No responsible gambling tooling. Absent or buried limit-setting and self-exclusion functions.
Sports bonuses, free bets and promotions at NC betting sites
Every offer on this page is one of a handful of structures. Learn the structures and you can evaluate any North Carolina sportsbook bonuses you encounter, here or elsewhere, in about ninety seconds.
Deposit match welcome bonuses
The most common format, and the one behind most offers listed above. You deposit, the book credits a percentage of that deposit as bonus funds, and those funds must be turned over a stated number of times before any associated winnings become withdrawable.
The decisive detail is the rollover base. "5x on deposit plus bonus" is a very different obligation from "5x on bonus." Here is an illustrative calculation using the outline's example figures — these are worked assumptions to demonstrate the math, not any specific operator's terms:
- Deposit $200, receive a $100 bonus, rollover 5x on bonus only: 5 × $100 = $500 in qualifying wagers.
- Same deposit and bonus, rollover 5x on deposit plus bonus: 5 × $300 = $1,500 in qualifying wagers.
- Same deposit and bonus at 10x on deposit plus bonus: 10 × $300 = $3,000 in qualifying wagers.
Identical headline figures, obligations ranging from $500 to $3,000. At $3,000 of turnover on a $200 deposit, you are betting your entire bankroll fifteen times over, and a normal house edge applies to every one of those wagers. That is the real cost of a large match, and it is why the smaller offers on this page are not automatically the worse ones.
Risk-free and second-chance wagers
A risk-free bet refunds your first losing wager, almost always as site credit rather than cash. The term is misleading enough that licensed US operators have largely stopped using it — "second chance bet" or "bonus back" is more accurate. You can absolutely lose money on one: if a $500 risk-free bet loses, you receive $500 in credit that itself carries turnover conditions, and if that credit loses too, your original $500 is gone. Check whether the refund arrives as one token or several, and what the expiry window is.
Free bets and stake-not-returned settlement
Free bets are the structure behind BetOnline's and Sportsbetting's offers, and behind the $50 free bet inside Lucky Rebel's package. Nearly all are stake-not-returned (SNR): the token's face value is not paid back with a win.
Worked example, illustrative: a $50 SNR free bet at +150 returns $75 in profit. A $50 cash bet at the same price returns $125 total — $75 profit plus your $50 stake. The free bet is worth $75 to you, not $125. As a rough rule, an SNR free bet is worth roughly 70–80% of its face value depending on the price you take it at, and taking it at a longer price generally extracts more value than taking it at a short favorite.
Reload bonuses for existing accounts
Reloads are percentage matches on subsequent deposits, usually smaller than the welcome offer — 25% to 50% is typical — and often tied to a day of the week, a funding method or a specific event. Over a full football season, a book with a steady reload program can be worth more than one with a large one-time welcome bonus and nothing afterward. Reloads carry their own rollover, frequently different from the welcome terms, and usually a much shorter claim window.
Reduced juice and reduced vig promotions
These are the offers that most directly reward price-sensitive bettors, because they improve your pricing rather than handing you credit. Standard pricing on a point spread or totals market is -110 a side. A reduced juice promotion might drop that to -105 or -102 on selected games.
The effect compounds. At -110 you risk $110 to win $100; at -105 you risk $105 for the same return. Across a hundred bets at $110 a side, the difference in what you stake is $500 — with no rollover, no expiry and no qualifying conditions attached. Reduced vig offers are usually limited to specific leagues or specific days, and sometimes to a maximum stake, so read the scope. For a bettor placing volume rather than chasing bonuses, a persistent reduced-juice program beats a headline match almost every time.
Odds boosts and enhanced prices
A boost raises the price on a pre-selected wager — a player prop, a parlay leg combination, a team to cover. Boosts are nearly always capped at a low maximum stake, often $25 to $50, and the boosted price still contains margin. A boost from +400 to +500 sounds substantial, but on a $25 cap that is $25 of extra potential return. Worth taking when the underlying wager is one you'd make anyway; not a reason to make a wager you otherwise wouldn't.
The conditions that decide whether any of this is worth claiming
- Minimum odds. Most bonuses require qualifying wagers at or above a stated price, commonly -200 or longer. A -400 favorite typically won't count toward rollover at all.
- Market exclusions. Live/in-play wagers, cashed-out bets, certain props and both sides of a two-way market are frequently excluded from turnover credit.
- Sports versus casino multiples. Sportsbook rollover commonly sits in the 5x–15x range; casino bonus rollover is usually far higher, 30x and up, with game weighting on top. Never assume a combined offer shares one number.
- Expiry. Welcome bonuses commonly run 14 to 30 days; free bets often 7 to 14; reloads sometimes 48 hours. Unused credit expires without notice.
- Maximum cashout. Some bonuses cap the amount of bonus-derived winnings you can withdraw regardless of what you accumulate.
- Cancellation before rollover. Requesting a withdrawal mid-rollover typically forfeits the entire bonus and often any winnings from it.
Best North Carolina sports betting promo codes and current offers
The advantage of a promo code is that it attaches you to a specific published offer rather than whatever default the site happens to show. It also creates a record of which terms you accepted, which matters if a dispute arises later. Enter the code at registration or at first deposit — most offers cannot be applied retroactively once a deposit has landed.
The five strongest offers across the books ranked on this page, judged on usable value rather than headline size:
- Lucky Rebel — 125% up to $1,250 plus a $50 free bet. The largest combined package here. The free bet component has clearer value than the match, which carries 10x turnover on the bonus amount.
- BetUS — 100% up to $2,000 on sports plus 25% on casino. The highest sports-specific ceiling. Evaluate the sports half on its own; the casino half carries substantially heavier terms.
- BetOnline — $250 in free bets. No deposit-match rollover to clear, just qualifying wagers per token. The simplest terms of any large offer on this page.
- BetNow — 125% up to $2,500. The biggest maximum in the ranking, and only relevant if you genuinely intend to deposit and turn over at that level.
- Bovada — 50% up to $250. The most clearable offer here. Low ceiling, low obligation, short path to a withdrawable balance.
Promotional terms change. Confirm the current conditions on the operator's own promotions page before depositing — the figures shown on the cards above this text reflect what was supplied to us, not a live feed.
Payment methods and cashier limits at NC online sportsbooks
Banking is where US-facing betting accounts differ most from ordinary online purchases. A deposit method working does not mean the same method works for withdrawal, and that asymmetry catches people out constantly. The table below covers the ten methods most commonly encountered. Treat it as general market guidance — specific limits, fees and availability vary by operator and must be confirmed in each book's own cashier.
| Method | Deposit | Withdrawal | Typical speed | Fee exposure | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Visa | Yes | Rarely | Instant deposit | Possible cash advance fee | 
| Mastercard | Yes | Rarely | Instant deposit | Possible cash advance fee | 
| American Express | Sometimes | No | Instant deposit | Higher decline rate | 
| Discover | Sometimes | No | Instant deposit | Varies by issuer | 
| Bitcoin (BTC) | Yes | Yes | Under 1 hour to same day | Network fee only | 
| Ethereum (ETH) | Yes | Yes | Minutes to same day | Gas fee | 
| Litecoin (LTC) | Yes | Yes | Minutes | Low network fee | 
| Solana (SOL) | Sometimes | Sometimes | Minutes | Very low network fee | 
| Stablecoins (USDT/USDC) | Yes | Yes | Minutes to same day | Network fee, chain-dependent | 
| Bank wire | Sometimes | Yes | 3–7 business days | Bank and operator fees likely | 
Visa and Mastercard
The default deposit route for most American bettors and the most familiar. Deposits post instantly when they go through — and the caveat matters, because US issuers decline gambling-coded transactions to offshore merchants at a meaningful rate. A decline is not evidence of a problem with the sportsbook; it is your bank's policy.
Two cautions. First, many issuers treat gambling deposits as cash advances, which means a separate fee, a higher interest rate, and interest accruing from day one with no grace period. Check your cardholder agreement before funding a betting account by credit card. Second, card deposits almost never support withdrawals back to the card at offshore books, so plan a separate payout route at the outset.
American Express and Discover
Accepted less widely than Visa and Mastercard, and with higher decline rates. Where a book does accept them, deposit behavior is the same as other cards, and the same cash advance risk applies. Neither is realistically a withdrawal channel. If you carry only an Amex or Discover card, verify acceptance in the cashier before registering rather than assuming it.
Bitcoin
The most widely supported crypto option at US-facing books and typically the fastest withdrawal route. Deposits confirm on-chain, usually within an hour depending on network conditions and the operator's required confirmation count. Withdrawals leave the operator once approved and settle at network speed.
Bitcoin's main drawback is volatility. Your sportsbook balance is denominated in USD, so the conversion happens when you deposit and again when you withdraw. Between those points, the BTC price can move — sometimes in your favor, sometimes not. Network fees also rise during congestion, which matters more on small transactions.
Ethereum
Broadly comparable to Bitcoin for betting purposes, with somewhat faster confirmation and gas fees that fluctuate with network demand. Same USD conversion consideration, same volatility exposure. Worth using if it is already your primary holding; not worth acquiring specifically for betting unless the operator offers a crypto-specific bonus premium.
Litecoin
Often the quiet best choice for moving money to and from a betting account. Confirmations are fast, network fees are consistently low, and it is supported nearly everywhere Bitcoin is. Litecoin carries the same price volatility risk as any non-pegged cryptocurrency, but the shorter time in transit reduces exposure.
Solana
Increasingly supported, with very fast settlement and negligible fees. Availability is less universal than the three above, so confirm support in the cashier before moving funds. Sending to an unsupported address or the wrong network is generally irreversible.
Stablecoins: USDT and USDC
For most bettors, stablecoins are the sensible crypto option. Because they are pegged to the US dollar, you get crypto settlement speed without the price exposure — $500 in USDT is still approximately $500 when you withdraw it. The critical detail is chain selection: USDT exists on multiple networks, and sending on a chain the operator does not support will lose the funds. Match the network exactly to what the cashier specifies, and send a small test transaction first if you are unsure.
Person-to-person transfers
Some US-facing books offer person-to-person money transfer services as a deposit and payout channel. These work through a third-party transfer network and typically involve manual steps — a reference code, a named recipient, a pickup or delivery process. Fees are usually higher than crypto, and the method is slower. Its niche is bettors who have neither a working card nor any crypto access. Limits tend to be modest and the process tends to be the one most often subject to additional verification.
Bank wire transfers
The channel for large payouts. Wires typically carry the highest minimum — often several hundred dollars — and both the operator and your receiving bank may charge fees. Settlement runs three to seven business days, and international wires can be held for additional compliance review at the receiving end. Where a wire does add real value is at the high end: it is often the only route for payouts above per-transaction crypto ceilings.
Currency conversion is worth a final note. Accounts at the books listed here are USD-denominated, so an American bettor funding with a US card typically incurs no FX cost. Crypto introduces conversion at both ends. Wires occasionally route through correspondent banks that apply their own charges. Check which conversions apply to your chosen route before assuming the number leaving your account equals the number arriving.
Withdrawals, KYC and payout processing explained
Payout timing has two separate stages, and conflating them is the most common source of frustration. Stage one is operator approval: your withdrawal request goes into a queue, gets reviewed against bonus status, account verification and risk rules, and is either approved or returned for more information. Stage two is network settlement: once approved, the money moves at the speed of the payment rail you chose.
An operator advertising "same-day crypto payouts" is describing stage two. If your request sits unapproved for three days because your ID documents are outstanding, the payment rail's speed is irrelevant. The variable you control is stage one — complete verification early.
Realistic timeframes by stage
- Approval queue: a few hours to several business days, depending on the operator, the amount, the day of the week and whether your account is fully verified.
- Crypto settlement after approval: minutes to a few hours. Litecoin and Solana are usually quickest; Bitcoin depends on network congestion.
- Bank wire settlement after approval: three to seven business days, sometimes longer for additional compliance checks.
- Person-to-person after approval: one to several business days including the collection step.
Why KYC applies even offshore
Bettors sometimes assume an internationally licensed book means no identity checks. It does not. Every licensing jurisdiction of any standing imposes anti-money-laundering obligations, and payment processors impose their own on top. Expect to verify identity before your first withdrawal clears, regardless of where the operator is licensed.
The documents typically requested are a government-issued photo ID (driver's license or passport), a proof of address dated within the last three months (utility bill or bank statement), and proof of ownership of your funding method — a card image with the middle digits obscured, or a screenshot of a crypto wallet. Some books request a selfie holding your ID.
Two practical points. Submit these when you open the account, not when you want your money. And make sure your registration details match your documents exactly: a nickname instead of a legal first name, or an old address, will stall verification and there is no way to shortcut it. Attempting to verify an account with someone else's documents is fraud and will cost you the balance.
Withdrawal fees and payout limits
Many US-facing books offer one free withdrawal per calendar month or per week, with a fee on additional requests. Crypto payouts carry network fees that may be absorbed by the operator or passed to you. Wires almost always carry fees at both ends.
Maximum payout limits exist in two forms: per-transaction caps and rolling period caps. A weekly cap matters far more than a transaction cap — if you win $20,000 and the weekly ceiling is $2,500, you are waiting eight weeks. Find both figures in the terms before you deposit, not after you win. This is one of the clearest differentiators between a reasonable operator and a predatory one.
Line errors, voided wagers and disputes
Every sportsbook's terms include an obvious-error or palpable-error clause allowing the void of wagers accepted at clearly incorrect prices — a mistyped spread, a line left open after a result, a market posted with the wrong participants. These clauses are standard and enforceable. What varies is how tightly defined they are. Terms specifying a threshold and a review process are better than terms permitting voids at sole discretion with no stated grounds.
If a dispute arises, the process runs: operator support first, in writing, with screenshots and bet IDs; then formal escalation through the operator's published complaints procedure; then, where one exists, the operator's licensing authority or any alternative dispute resolution body it names. For books outside the NCSLC framework, there is no state-level route. That is a real limitation and you should factor it into the decision before depositing rather than discovering it afterward.
Sports and leagues available at North Carolina betting sites
Market breadth varies between the books listed here, but the core coverage is consistent across all of them. What differs is depth — how many props per game, how far out the futures run, how many in-play markets stay open late in a contest.
Major US leagues and college sports
College sport carries disproportionate weight here, and any honest assessment of a book for this audience has to start there. UNC Tar Heels, Duke Blue Devils, NC State Wolfpack and Wake Forest Demon Deacons basketball drive enormous local volume from November through March, and the ACC schedule is the single most-watched betting calendar in the state. Depth on college basketball — player props, first-half lines, alternate spreads, conference tournament futures — is a more useful discriminator between books here than NFL coverage, which is uniformly good everywhere.
College football matters too, with the ACC slate and bowl season drawing steady action. On the professional side, the Carolina Panthers (NFL), Charlotte Hornets (NBA), Carolina Hurricanes (NHL) and Charlotte FC (MLS) anchor local interest. MLB coverage runs daily through the summer with run lines, totals and pitcher props. NHL betting has grown alongside the Hurricanes, with puck lines, goal totals and shots-on-goal props standard. UFC and boxing are covered across all the books here, typically with method-of-victory and round markets alongside the moneyline.
NASCAR and horse racing
NASCAR is a local specialty. The Coca-Cola 600 at Charlotte Motor Speedway is one of the biggest betting events on the state's calendar, and coverage typically includes outright winners, head-to-head matchups, top-five and top-ten finishes, manufacturer markets and stage winners.
Horse racing is handled differently from other sports. Some books offer a full racebook with pari-mutuel wagering into the track pools; others offer fixed-odds racing on selected meetings; some offer nothing at all. If racing is a priority, confirm which of the three applies at your chosen book rather than assuming a racebook exists because other sports are covered.
Soccer, international and niche markets
Soccer is the broadest international category — Premier League, Champions League, MLS including Charlotte FC, Liga MX and major tournaments — with match result, both-teams-to-score, corners, cards and goalscorer markets. Tennis runs year-round through the four majors and the tour calendar. Golf coverage centers on the majors and weekly PGA Tour events with outrights, matchups and top-finish markets. Esports appears at most of these books with CS2, League of Legends and Dota 2 coverage, though depth varies considerably. Novelty and entertainment markets appear seasonally; availability of political markets depends on the operator and its licensing jurisdiction, and should not be assumed.
Odds formats, wager types and pricing at NC sportsbooks
Pricing is where a sportsbook quietly costs or saves you money, and it deserves more attention than bonus size. The books here display American odds by default, with decimal and fractional usually available in settings.
- American odds. A minus number is the stake required to win $100 (-110 means risk $110 to win $100). A plus number is the profit on a $100 stake (+150 means $100 returns $150 profit).
- Decimal odds. Total return per unit staked, stake included. -110 converts to 1.91; +150 converts to 2.50.
- Fractional odds. Profit relative to stake. +150 is 3/2; -110 is roughly 10/11.
- Moneyline. Straight pick of the winner, no spread involved. The standard entry wager.
- Point spread. A handicap applied to level the contest, typically priced -110 a side. The default wager type for football and basketball.
- Totals (over/under). Combined score above or below a posted number, again usually -110 a side.
- Parlays. Multiple selections combined into one wager; all must win. Returns multiply, and so does the book's margin on every leg.
- Same-game parlays (SGP). Correlated legs from a single contest. Priced using correlation models rather than simple multiplication, which usually means a higher effective hold than a standard parlay.
- Teasers. Parlays where you move each spread or total in your favor by a set number of points in exchange for a reduced payout. Common in football at six, 6.5 and seven points.
- Props. Wagers on outcomes within a contest — player points, passing yards, strikeouts, shots on goal, or team props like first to score.
- Futures. Long-term markets: championship winners, conference titles, season win totals, individual awards. Your stake is tied up until settlement.
- Live/in-play betting. Wagering after the event starts, with prices updating continuously. Bet acceptance delays and suspensions are normal.
- Cash out. Settling an open wager early at a price the book offers. Convenient, but the offered price always contains margin — you are paying for certainty.
Vig, line movement and limits
The -110 standard exists because it contains the book's margin. Two sides at -110 means the book collects $220 in stakes and pays out $210, holding roughly 4.5% on a balanced market. Reduced juice offerings at -105 cut that materially, which is why they are worth more to a high-volume bettor than most bonuses.
Lines move for two reasons: new information (injuries, weather, lineup news) and money (one side attracting disproportionate stakes). Different books move at different speeds, which creates the price differences that line-shopping bettors exploit. Holding accounts at multiple books is the single most practical way to improve your effective pricing.
Betting limits vary by book, by market and by account. Major league sides carry the highest ceilings; props and niche markets carry much lower ones. Some operators reduce limits on accounts they judge to be consistently beating their lines — a policy that exists across the industry and is rarely disclosed in advance. If high limits matter to you, ask support directly before committing a bankroll.
One caution on interpretation: a large market count is a marketing statistic, not a reliability indicator. A book advertising thousands of markets per game tells you nothing about whether it settles promptly, prices competitively or pays out reliably. Software stability during peak live events — an ACC rivalry game, NFL Sunday afternoon — is a more meaningful test, and it is not something a market count reveals.
NC mobile sports betting: apps and browser play
The mobile betting experience
Most wagering here happens on a phone, and the mobile interface is where a sportsbook's quality is most visible. The things worth checking: how quickly the live betting page refreshes during a fast-moving game, whether bet acceptance is prompt or subject to long confirmation delays, how many taps it takes to build a same-game parlay, and whether the cashier is fully usable on mobile — including deposits and withdrawal requests in USD or crypto.
The books ranked on this page generally support both iOS and Android through mobile-optimized sites. Biometric login via FaceID or TouchID depends on the specific platform and how it is installed; where it is available it is a genuine convenience for a book you use daily.
Browser play versus progressive web apps
An important distinction, and one that is frequently blurred. State-licensed operators here distribute native apps through the Apple App Store and Google Play. Internationally licensed books — including every operator on this page — generally do not appear in those stores, because store policies restrict gambling apps by jurisdiction.
Instead, these books run responsive mobile websites, often installable to your home screen as a progressive web app. A PWA gets you an icon, a full-screen view and app-like navigation, but it is still a website running in a browser container. It is not a native app store download, and we will not describe it as one. In practice the difference is modest for betting purposes, though PWAs are more dependent on connection quality and may handle push notifications differently. If you specifically require a store-downloaded native app, none of the books listed here will provide one — verify in the cashier and on the operator's own site rather than relying on a comparison page for that detail.
Retail sportsbooks and tribal venues across the state
Online is not the whole picture, and the physical side of the market is structurally connected to the mobile one.
Tribal casinos and retail sportsbooks
Retail sports wagering here began on tribal land, under federal Indian gaming law and tribal-state compacts rather than under Chapter 18C. Harrah's Cherokee Casino Resort and Harrah's Cherokee Valley River, both operated by the Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians, opened retail sportsbooks before commercial mobile wagering existed. The Catawba Nation's Two Kings Casino in Kings Mountain operates under its own tribal framework.
These are legally distinct from commercial mobile operators. They are regulated through tribal gaming authorities and compact arrangements, not by the NCSLC in the same way a commercial mobile licensee is. A bettor's practical experience — walk in, place a cash wager at a counter or kiosk, collect winnings on site — differs accordingly, with no account, no app and no geolocation involved.
Sports venue retail lounges
The Sports Wagering Act also permits retail sportsbook facilities at qualifying commercial venues. The qualifying sites named in the framework are the state's major professional and motorsports venues — Charlotte Motor Speedway, Bank of America Stadium, Spectrum Center, PNC Arena and comparable facilities. These lounges are operated by licensed commercial operators in partnership with the venue.
Why land-based partnerships underpin the mobile market
Here is the connection that makes the whole structure make sense. The Act does not permit a mobile operator to obtain a license on its own. Each mobile license must be tethered to a qualifying land-based partner — a professional franchise, a major venue, a motorsports facility or a tribal gaming operation. The partnership is the licensing gateway.
That design choice explains the shape of the licensed market: a limited number of national operators, each visibly attached to a recognizable local partner, rather than an unlimited field of applicants. It also ties a share of the economic benefit to in-state sports organizations. Offshore operators, having no such partnership and no license, sit entirely outside this structure.
Responsible gambling tools and support in North Carolina
Betting is entertainment with a real and recurring cost. Most bettors lose over time — that is how the margin described in the pricing section works. Never wager money you need for anything else, and never treat betting as a way to recover a loss or resolve a financial problem.
Tools worth setting up on day one, before they feel necessary:
- Deposit limits — daily, weekly or monthly ceilings on what you can fund.
- Wager limits — caps on stake size or total amount staked in a period.
- Loss limits — a ceiling on net losses over a defined window.
- Session timers — reminders or automatic logouts after a set period.
- Cool-off periods — short account locks, typically 24 hours to several weeks.
- Self-exclusion — longer or permanent account closure that cannot be reversed on request.
An important limitation: self-exclusion at one sportsbook does not automatically apply elsewhere. It may extend across sister sites under the same parent company, but that depends entirely on the operator's own policy and is not guaranteed. The statewide voluntary exclusion program administered through the NCSLC framework covers licensed operators — it does not reach operators outside that framework. If you self-exclude, exclude at every book you hold an account with, and consider device-level blocking software as well. Never attempt to work around a self-exclusion, a verification check or an account restriction.
Free, confidential help is available now:
- North Carolina Problem Gambling Program (NCPGP): 1-877-718-5543 — the state helpline, available 24/7.
- National Problem Gambling Helpline: 1-800-GAMBLER — operated by the National Council on Problem Gambling, 24/7, with call, text and chat options.
- SAMHSA National Helpline: 1-800-662-4357 — free, confidential treatment referral and information, 24/7.
Our responsible gambling resources page has more detail on limit-setting and support options.
Choosing between these North Carolina sportsbooks
Use the evidence on this page in a specific order. Start with licensing status and whether the absence of NCSLC oversight is acceptable to you — that is a threshold question, not a scoring factor. Then look at pricing and whether reduced juice is available on the markets you actually bet. Then check bonus terms, specifically the rollover base and multiple rather than the headline figure. Then confirm your payment route works in both directions, and find the weekly payout cap before you deposit. Finally, check that the mobile experience and market depth match how you bet — heavy ACC basketball props are a different requirement from NFL sides only.
Bigger bonuses on this page generally carry heavier obligations; smaller ones clear faster. Neither is universally better — the right choice depends on your volume. You can read more about how we work on our about page, or get in touch through our contact page. Our terms and conditions set out the basis on which this information is published.
You must be 21 or older to wager on sports in North Carolina. Tax and legal points on this page are general information only — consult a qualified tax professional or attorney about your own circumstances. If gambling stops being entertainment, call 1-877-718-5543 or 1-800-GAMBLER.

Sex Overseas: 'What Soldiers Do' Complicates WWII History
Americans often think of World War II as the "good war," but historian Mary Louise Roberts says her new book might make our understanding of that conflict "more truthful and more complex." The book, What Soldiers Do: Sex and the American GI in World War II France, tells the story of relations between American men and French women in Normandy and elsewhere.
The Americans were liberators; the French were liberated. But sex created tensions and resentments that were serious, yet were utterly absent from contemporary accounts for American audiences back home. Roberts, who is professor of European history at the University of Wisconsin, Madison, suggests that the tensions weren't entirely accidental: "Sex was fundamental to how the U.S. military framed, fought and won the war in Europe," she writes in her book.
Roberts joins NPR's Robert Siegel to talk about prostitutes in parks and cemeteries, pinups on planes and how the U.S. Army responded to rape accusations with rapid, racially charged trials.
Interview Highlights
On the familiar image of grateful Normans and respectful GIs
"I think it's a matter of chronology. I think that initially the Normans were incredibly grateful to be liberated. They had also suffered a lot of loss that summer, so there was some anger about the destruction of their homes and the loss of their loved ones. But in general, at least at the beginning, the French were very happy to be liberated and to greet the Americas."
On the mayor of Le Havre complaining about American GIs having sex in public with French prostitutes
"That happened in the summer of 1945, so a year [after liberation]. Le Havre was a port, really the entry and exit port for millions of American soldiers during those years. Those soldiers who had been fighting in France and Germany came back to Le Havre waiting for a boat home. They were, as a group, exhausted and traumatized. Their lost friends crowded their dreams. They were consumed by guilt. So they took to whoring with French women as a way to keep away the demons, at least for a while. And without a proper or regulated system of brothels, they instead took to the streets, abandoned buildings, parks and cemeteries having sex."
On whether the behavior of World War II GIs was universal to soldiers or specific to that army in that war
"It was a particularly eroticized war. Anybody who remembers the pinups on airplanes, Rita Hayworth, the amount to which pinups became a part of the culture of the GIs, will recognize to what extent sex became important to the war experience. I went and looked at Stars and Stripes, which is the trench journal, and what I saw there was an extension of the pinup culture. Photojournalism in particular was used to portray the Frenchwoman as ready to be rescued, ready to greet the American soldier and ready to congratulate and thank him through a kiss or even more."
On French women traveling to Normandy to prostitute themselves
"I would have to say that prostitution was pervasive in the European theater. There was one Army report that estimated 80 percent of single men and 50 percent of married men would have sex during their stay in Europe. And the U.S. military did not really care that much that it occurred. What it cared about was venereal disease, which soon after the GIs' arrivals in France began to soar — but all this was kept from the American public."
On a wave of rape accusations in the summer of 1944, and how the U.S. Army's response was to frame it as a race problem
"What happened was the American Army and the [Judge Advocate General] office disproportionately blamed African-American soldiers. Seventy-seven percent of the court-martial prosecutions in the European theater were for African-Americans. They were only 10 percent of the troops. ...
"[Trials took place] sometimes three days afterwards. ... Many of the men were [hanged] in the towns where the rape, alleged rape, occurred. And the hanging was a difficult thing to do in the land of the guillotine, so the U.S. Army actually brought in their own hangman from Texas. I found a file in the National Archives which dealt with this. ... Grisly, very grisly."
On how she integrates the heroism and great military accomplishments with the behavior of troops in France
"I guess like many people I was somewhat surprised when I found out that the GIs were not impeccable soldiers. I began to look at documents in France that were only opened in January of 2005, and in many cases I was the first American to look at them.
"I grew up in a very patriotic family, my father is a veteran of the Second World War, so all this was difficult for me. But I actually also have to say that there's nothing in my book that tries to condemn or denigrate that great moment. What I'm trying to do is give a fuller picture by looking at how the event was seen by the French, to make it richer and more complex — and to me really good history portrays an event not in a sanitized way, but as a way in which you can allow yourself to think of soldiers as human beings."
article_title: Sex Overseas: 'What Soldiers Do' Complicates WWII History

Satellite photo shows Russian troops were stationed in Chernobyl's radioactive zone
Loading...
During its occupation of the Chernobyl nuclear site, Russia appears to have stationed troops in an area of high radioactive contamination, according to new satellite imagery obtained by NPR from the company Planet.
The decision raises the possibility that Russia exposed its own soldiers to potentially unhealthy levels of radioactivity during its month-plus possession of the defunct nuclear facility.
Experts say the levels are not nearly enough to cause sudden radiation poisoning, but they could potentially elevate the long-term risks of cancer for the soldiers.
"You shouldn't go into a contaminated site and have people camping out and digging in the dirt," says Kathryn Higley, a radiation health physicist at Oregon State University. While the risk of developing cancer in the long term remains "very, very low," she says it shows Russia's disregard for the well-being of its own troops.
A risky stopping place for troops
Chernobyl was the site of the world's worst nuclear disaster in 1986. A meltdown and explosion spewed radioactive material across the region, and fallout throughout Western Europe. Nearly 40 years after the accident, an exclusion zone — where people are prohibited from living or growing crops — remains in effect around the nuclear plant.
The satellite image shows an apparent Russian convoy and encampment in one of the more radioactive parts of the exclusion zone — on the edge of the so-called "red forest" — a region so contaminated by the nuclear meltdown that most of the trees died at the time. The image, dated from March 16, shows the convoy of around 30 vehicles parked on a stretch of road about 3.5 kilometers (2.2 miles) west of the ruined reactor. Nearby appears what looks like a small encampment, with berms, trenches for armored vehicles and a tent (location: 51.3892, 30.0479).
Loading...
An image from March 28, days before Russia's withdrawal from Chernobyl and the surrounding exclusion zone, shows fires burning near the site of the encampment. A second image, from March 29, shows that the fire reached the camp and may have destroyed it before being extinguished.
Ukraine's state utility, Energatom, posted drone footage of the same site on its Telegram channel on April 6. That footage shows the charred area, along with the remains of what appear to be temporary buildings, as well as trenches and sandbag positions on the road.
The International Atomic Energy says that it is aware of the reports that Russian troops may have been exposed to radiation, but so far it has been unable to verify them.
"The IAEA has reviewed the footage but can only undertake an independent radiological assessment once its experts are on the site," the agency said in a statement on Thursday.
The exclusion zone around Chernobyl is subject to wildfires this time of year, and it remains unclear whether the fire was natural, a result of activities by Russian troops or deliberately started by someone else.
Russia seized Chernobyl in late February, and held the site for over a month.
Rumors of radioactive poisoning spread
Since the withdrawal of Russian forces on March 31, rumors have been circulating on social media that its troops at Chernobyl had fallen ill after digging trenches on the site. A post on a Belarusian Telegram channel that monitors troop activity inside the country showed military vehicles arriving at a hospital in the city of Gomel, which specializes in treating radiation.
NPR was able to identify the location of a photo in the Belarussian post as being taken at the hospital, but was not able to verify whether the vehicles or their passengers were Russian. The Telegram channel also noted that Russian troops are regularly seen at the facility.
The area in Chernobyl that was used by the Russian troops "is decently hot," according to Tim Mousseau, an ecologist at the University of South Carolina who's studied the Chernobyl exclusion zone for years.
But Mousseau and Higley both say that the troops couldn't have gotten radiation poisoning from living on the site, even for a month.
"It seems unlikely that a very large dose would be received from just sitting in the trenches," Mousseau told NPR via email. "A more likely scenario, based on having brought dozens of visitors to the zone with me over the years, is that there was a psychosomatic response to finding out that they were in a highly contaminated region."
Loading...
Higley adds that the Russian soldiers may have been experiencing other health issues as well. "It could be stress, it could be cold, it could be bad food; all of those things can mimic the symptoms of radiation syndrome," she says.
Higley says that the decision to station forces in the forests around Chernobyl is "only one small bad thing on a list of a whole lot of other bad things" being done by Russia in Ukraine. Even the troops who slept there face far larger risks if they are redeployed to forward positions in eastern Ukraine, where Russia is reportedly sending reinforcements.
"In the grand scheme of things," she says, "I think a little bit of radiation risk from sleeping on the ground at Chernobyl is probably the least of their worries at this point."
NPR's Koko Nakajima and Tien Le contributed to this report.
article_title: Satellite photo shows Russian troops were stationed in Chernobyl's radioactive zone

Video analysis reveals Russian attack on Ukrainian nuclear plant veered near disaster
Loading...
Last week's assault by Russian forces on the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant was far more dangerous than initial assessments suggested, according to an analysis by NPR of video and photographs of the attack and its aftermath.
A thorough review of a four-hour, 21-minute security camera video of the attack reveals that Russian forces repeatedly fired heavy weapons in the direction of the plant's massive reactor buildings, which housed dangerous nuclear fuel. Photos show that an administrative building directly in front of the reactor complex was shredded by Russian fire. And a video from inside the plant shows damage and a possible Russian shell that landed less than 250 feet from the Unit 2 reactor building.
The security camera footage also shows Russian troops haphazardly firing rocket-propelled grenades into the main administrative building at the plant and turning away Ukrainian firefighters even as a fire raged out of control in a nearby training building.
The evidence stands in stark contrast to early comments by the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), which while acknowledging the seriousness of the assault, emphasized that the action took place away from the reactors. In a news conference immediately after the attack, IAEA Director-General Rafael Mariano Grossi made reference to only a single projectile hitting a training building adjacent to the reactor complex.
"All the safety systems of the six reactors at the plant were not affected at all," Grossi told reporters at the March 4 briefing.
In fact, the training building took multiple strikes, and it was hardly the only part of the site to take fire from Russian forces. The security footage supports claims by Ukraine's nuclear regulator of damage at three other locations: the Unit 1 reactor building, the transformer at the Unit 6 reactor and the spent fuel pad, which is used to store nuclear waste. It also shows ordnance striking a high-voltage line outside the plant. The IAEA says two such lines were damaged in the attack.
"This video is very disturbing," says Edwin Lyman, director of nuclear power safety at the Union of Concerned Scientists. While the types of reactors used at the plant are far safer than the one that exploded in Chernobyl in 1986, the Russian attack could have triggered a meltdown similar to the kind that struck Japan's Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant in 2011, he warns.
"It's completely insane to subject a nuclear plant to this kind of an assault," Lyman says.
In a news conference on Thursday, Grossi said that he had met with Ukrainian and Russian officials but failed to reach an agreement to avoid future attacks on Ukraine's other nuclear plants. "I'm aiming at having something relatively soon," he told reporters in Vienna.
The assault
On March 3, the nuclear plant was preparing for a fight. A news release posted to its website just hours before the assault described the facility as operating normally, with its assigned Ukrainian military unit ready for combat.
The Russian decision to move on the plant was clearly premeditated, according to Leone Hadavi, an open-source analyst with the Centre for Information Resilience, who helped NPR review the video.
"It was planned," Hadavi says, and it involved around 10 armored vehicles as well as two tanks. That is far more firepower than would have been carried by, say, a reconnaissance mission that might have stumbled across the plant by chance.
Just before 11:30 p.m. local time, someone began livestreaming the plant's security footage on its YouTube channel. The livestream rolled on as Russian forces began a slow and methodical advance on the plant. The column of armored vehicles, led by the tanks, used spotlights to cautiously approach the plant from the southeast along the main service road to the facility.
Loading...
Around an hour and 20 minutes later, one of the two tanks that led the column was struck by a missile from Ukrainian forces and was disabled.
That marked the beginning of a fierce firefight that lasted for roughly two hours at the plant. Immediately after the tank was disabled, Russian forces returning fire appeared to hit a transmission line connected to the plant's main electrical substation. The IAEA says two of four high-voltage lines were damaged in the attack. Lyman says that these lines are essential to safe operations at the plant.
Loading...
Russian forces then pushed their way into the parking area near the front gate and began shooting.
Much of the fire was directed toward the training center and the plant's main administrative building. But at various points in the battle, Russian forces lobbed rounds deep into the nuclear complex in the direction of the reactor buildings.
Loading...
It's unclear whether the Russian troops were deliberately trying to strike more sensitive sections of the plant or whether they were returning fire from Ukrainian forces off camera. But what is clear is that the shooting was not accidental.
"We don't see random volleys of fire," Hadavi says. "The fire is very concentrated. They clearly want to hit Point A, Point B, Point C and Point D."
The afternoon after the battle, the State Nuclear Regulatory Inspectorate of Ukraine reported that the reactor compartment of Unit 1, which lay in the direction of some of the Russian fire, had sustained damage. It also reported that two shells had landed in an area used to hold old nuclear waste that lay to the north of the battle. Later statements by the regulator and the IAEA reported further damage to the power transformer for the Unit 6 reactor.
At one point, the video shows Russian forces directing their firepower northward toward Unit 6 and the spent fuel area, corroborating those reports.
Hadavi says the Russian troops remained disciplined through most of their attack. Toward the end of the fight, however, some Russian soldiers seemed to be discharging rocket-propelled grenades indiscriminately toward the main administrative building. One was seen stepping from behind an armored vehicle, raising the weapon and — without kneeling to take careful aim — firing it into the upper floors of the building. A total of five rocket-propelled grenades were lobbed into the facility.
Loading...
Firefighters denied entry
By 2:25 a.m. on March 4, the fighting was largely over. Reinforcements arrived, including a Russian-built MRAP armored vehicle with a gray paint job resembling those used by the Russian National Guard.
Firefighting vehicles arrived at around 2:50 a.m., likely from the nearby town of Enerhodar. But even as the fire raged in the training building, Russian forces apparently forced the firefighters to turn around.
Loading...
The damage
In the days after the assault, Energoatom, the Ukrainian state-owned utility that ran Zaporizhzhia, released several photos showing damage to the site on the social media platform Telegram. Most notably, a short video shows what might be a Russian artillery shell on an elevated walkway leading toward the Unit 2 reactor building.
The possible shell was heavily damaged and could not be identified with confidence, but Hadavi says it bears resemblance to some 100 mm and 125 mm munitions used by Russian armored vehicles and tanks. The video also shows two holes that were punched through the walkway's ceiling, presumably by Russian fire, and damage to the steel beams holding up the roof.
Loading...
The location of the possible shell and the damage is within just a few hundred feet of the Unit 2 reactor building, says Tom Bielefeld, an independent nuclear security analyst based in Germany.
Bielefeld says that the walkway also runs alongside a building used to handle radioactive waste from the plant. That building is not as hardened, or reinforced against attacks and other catastrophic events, as the nuclear reactor buildings are. Had it been struck, there would have been the potential for a localized release of radioactive contamination.
"It was a near miss," Bielefeld says.
Energoatom also released several photos of battle damage to offices at the plant. NPR was able to verify the location as the main administrative building at the front of the facility.
Based on photos and damage assessments by Ukrainian officials and the IAEA, Lyman says that the damage appears to have been to some of the less hardened points within the nuclear plant. Unlike office buildings and elevated walkways, the reactors themselves and their spent fuel are sealed within a thick steel containment vessel that would withstand a great deal of damage.
But he also says that the host of systems required to keep the reactors safe are not hardened against attack. Cooling systems rely on exterior pipework; backup generators are kept in relatively ordinary buildings; vital electrical yards are out in the open; and the plant's control rooms are not designed to operate in a war zone.
Lyman says that the reactors at Zaporizhzhia have an inherently safer design than the ones at Chernobyl, which in 1986 was the site of the worst nuclear disaster the world has ever seen.
Nevertheless, he said, if the firefight had damaged more of the plant's critical subsystems and the nuclear engineers on-site hadn't been able to reach emergency backups, the situation could have turned dire.
"In a couple of hours, you have core damage starting and a situation that is potentially irreversible," he says. "And then you have Fukushima."
In 2011, at the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant in Japan, a massive tsunami disabled electrical and cooling systems. Without cooling, the cores of the three operating reactors overheated and the nuclear fuel eventually melted. The ensuing meltdown breached the containment vessels, and radioactive material spilled into the environment. Over 100,000 people were forced to evacuate from their homes for a prolonged period, and thousands have yet to return.
"Dangerous idiocy"
That did not happen at the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant, which is now firmly under Russian control. Russian state media showed off the capture of the plant on Wednesday while carefully framing out some of the damage Russian troops had caused. Meanwhile, Ukraine's nuclear inspectorate says that reactors 1 and 6 at the site have been effectively disabled by the fighting. A lack of personnel and parts is hindering scheduled maintenance at Unit 1 and repairs to the damaged Unit 6 transformer, respectively.
"We emphasize that incomplete and/or untimely implementation of maintenance measures for equipment important to safety can decrease its reliability and in turn lead to its failure and emergencies and accidents," the regulator said in a statement.
Bielefeld says he is deeply worried about the prospects of firefights at Ukraine's three remaining nuclear power stations. At Rivne Nuclear Power Plant in the country's north, the plant's director, Pavlo Pavlyshyn, told NPR that Ukrainian forces were prepared to mount a defense should Russian troops try to take the plant. And Russian forces are now advancing toward a second plant, the South Ukraine Nuclear Power Station.
"I hope this will be the last time we have to talk about these things," Bielefeld says. "But this war is not over yet."
Without some sort of rules of engagement regarding nuclear facilities, he worries that a more serious accident could be just a matter of time.
"Everybody knows that nuclear reactors are not designed to withstand all-out military assaults," he says. "It is dangerous idiocy."
NPR's Tim Mak and Daniel Wood contributed to this report.

WADA Compliance Review Committee recommends series of strong consequences for RUSADA non-compliance
WADA Executive Committee to consider recommendation and proposed consequences on 9 December
Having considered a report from the World Anti-Doping Agency’s (WADA’s) Intelligence and Investigations Department (I&I) and independent forensic experts, WADA’s independent Compliance Review Committee (CRC) has recommended to WADA’s Executive Committee (ExCo) that the Russian Anti-Doping Agency (RUSADA) be declared non-compliant with the World Anti-Doping Code (Code), as announced by WADA on 22 November 2019. This recommendation is accompanied by strong proposed consequences and conditions of reinstatement.
The CRC’s recommendation was delivered to the ExCo in accordance with the agreed process under the International Standard for Code Compliance by Signatories (ISCCS). Because the contents of the document have since appeared in part in the media, WADA is now making the following details of the CRC recommendation public. The ExCo will consider the recommendation at a specially convened meeting in Paris** on 9 December 2019.
CRC recommendation in relation to non-compliance with data requirement
The 26-page CRC recommendation, which is signed by CRC Chair, Jonathan Taylor QC, reminds the ExCo that as part of the 20 September 2018 decision to reinstate RUSADA to the list of Code-compliant Signatories, “WADA’s ExCo deemed the requirement to provide an authentic copy of the Moscow Data to be 'Critical' because:
- it would enable the anti-doping community finally to resolve and draw a line under the allegations of a systematic conspiracy to dope Russian athletes;
- it would ensure that any Russian athletes who had tested positive could be punished; and
- just as importantly it would ensure that innocent Russian athletes could be cleared of suspicion.”
The WADA I&I report was based in particular on a forensic review of inconsistencies found in some of the data that were obtained by WADA from the Moscow Laboratory in January 2019. Following WADA’s decision on 17 September 2019 to open a formal compliance procedure against RUSADA, this review also included consideration of responses from the Russian authorities to a list of detailed and technical questions raised by WADA I&I and the independent forensic experts.
Based on the reports issued by WADA I&I and the experts at the conclusion of their review, the CRC determined that:
- The Moscow data are neither complete nor fully authentic. In particular, while the 2019 copy of the Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) database matches in many respects the 2015 copy of the LIMS database provided to WADA by a whistleblower in 2017, hundreds of presumptive adverse analytical findings that appear in the 2015 copy of the LIMS database have been removed from the 2019 copy, and the related underlying raw data and PDF files have been deleted or altered.
- Some of the presumptive positive findings and related evidence were removed in 2016 or 2017, after the general scheme to cover up the doping of Russian athletes was first revealed by Dr Rodchenkov and then quickly confirmed by Prof. Richard McLaren's investigation (Part 1 and Part 2). However, further significant deletions and/or alterations were made in December 2018 and January 2019 (i.e., after the WADA ExCo imposed the data requirement). These activities were concealed by back-dating of computer systems and data files in an attempt to make it appear that the Moscow data had been in their current state since 2015. Furthermore, the commands issued to execute the manipulations, deletions and back-dating were also deleted, in an attempt to avoid detection of what had been done.
- In addition, on or after 25 November 2018 (i.e., again, after the data requirement was imposed), but before 10 January 2019 (i.e., before the Moscow data were made available to the WADA team), someone in the Moscow Laboratory:
- planted fabricated evidence into the LIMS database (purported messages between laboratory staff members) to support the argument now being advanced by the Russian authorities that it was Dr. Grigory Rodchenkov and two co-conspirators who falsified entries in the Moscow LIMS database as part of a scheme to extort money from athletes; and
- deleted from the LIMS database important evidence proving that another laboratory staff member was involved in the cover-up of doping by Russian athletes in 2014 and 2015. That staff member is currently an important witness for the Russian side in several cases, in which he denies there was any conspiracy to protect Russian athletes from exposure for doping, and calls Dr. Rodchenkov a liar.
The CRC concluded that this is “an extremely serious case of non-compliance with the requirement to provide an authentic copy of the Moscow data, with several aggravating features”.
CRC recommendation in relation to consequences (abridged)
The CRC has therefore recommended that WADA send a formal notice to RUSADA, asserting non-compliance with the requirement to provide an authentic copy of the Moscow data, and proposing the following consequences, to come into effect on the date on which the decision that RUSADA is non-compliant becomes final and to remain in effect until the fourth anniversary of that date (‘the Four Year Period’):
- Russian Government officials/representatives may not be appointed to sit and may not sit as members of the boards or committees or any other bodies of any Code Signatory (or its members) or association of Signatories.
- Russian Government officials/representatives may not participate in or attend any of the following events held in the Four Year Period: (a) the Youth Olympic Games (summer and winter); (b) the Olympic Games and Paralympic Games (summer and winter); (c) any other event organized by a Major Event Organisation; and (d) any World Championships organized or sanctioned by any Signatory (together, the Major Events).
- Russia may not host in the Four Year Period, or bid for or be granted in the Four Year Period, the right to host (whether during or after the Four Year Period) any editions of the Major Events.
- Where the right to host a Major Event in the Four Year Period has already been awarded to Russia, the Signatory must withdraw that right and re-assign the event to another country, unless it is legally or practically impossible to do so. In addition, Russia may not bid for the right to host the 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games, irrespective of whether the bidding takes place during or after the Four Year Period.
- Russia’s flag may not be flown at any Major Event staged in the Four Year Period.
- Neither the President, the Secretary-General, the CEO, nor any member of the Executive Board/Governing Board of either the Russian Olympic Committee or the Russian Paralympic Committee may participate in or attend any Major Event staged in the Four Year Period.
- Russian athletes and their support personnel may only participate in Major Events staged in the Four Year Period where they are able to demonstrate that they are not implicated in any way by the non-compliance (i.e., they are not mentioned in incriminating circumstances in the McLaren reports, there are no positive findings reported for them in the database, and no data relating to their samples has been manipulated), in accordance with strict conditions to be defined by WADA (or the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), if it sees fit), pursuant to the mechanism foreseen in ISCCS Article 11.2.6. In this circumstance, they may not represent the Russian Federation.
- Given the aggravating factors that are present in this case, RUSADA must pay all WADA’s costs on this file incurred since January 2019 and, in addition, a fine to WADA of 10% of its 2019 income or USD 100,000 (whichever is lower). This is the maximum fine available under the rules.
CRC recommendation concerning RUSADA’s operations
The CRC recommendation states that “the evidence (including from WADA's recent audits of RUSADA's operations) indicates that RUSADA’s work is effective in contributing to the fight against doping in Russian sport, and that it is working productively in cooperation with other Anti-Doping Organizations, including in investigations within Russia. Therefore, the CRC does not recommend any special monitoring or supervision or takeover of RUSADA's anti-doping activities in the Four Year Period.”
However, one of the conditions of reinstatement is that WADA Management remains satisfied throughout the Four Year Period that RUSADA’s independence is being respected and there is no improper outside interference with its operations.
Next steps
On 9 December 2019, WADA’s ExCo will meet to discuss the CRC’s recommendation. If the ExCo accepts the recommendation, formal notice will be sent to RUSADA, alleging non-compliance and proposing the above consequences, in accordance with the Code. RUSADA will have 21 days to accept the notice. If RUSADA does not accept it, the matter will be referred to CAS. If CAS imposes the proposed consequences, they will be binding and must be recognized and enforced by all Signatories.
** Following this media release, the Agency switched the ExCo meeting venue from Paris, France to Lausanne, Switzerland due to announced strike action in the French capital.
article_title: WADA Compliance Review Committee recommends series of strong consequences for RUSADA non-compliance
